correctness.rationale: The exact 12-vertex, 24-edge Chvatal graph is specified without a library labeling. A new, separately written enumerator reconstructed the 2,835 nonempty matchings, face vector (24,204,752,1175,628,52), 1,397 disjoint discrete-Morse pairs and an acyclic orientation of all 10,816 nonempty Hasse incidences. The surviving one-vertex CW complex has 34 cells in dimension 3 and 6 in dimension 4. An independent signed gradient-boundary computation recovered the exact 5x5 unimodular minor -1, 6x6 determinant 3, rank 5 modulo 3 and rank 6 modulo 2 and 5; hence the Smith factors are (1,1,1,1,1,3). The three-skeleton is a wedge of 34 three-spheres and is 2-connected; Hurewicz classifies all four-cell attaching maps by the columns of this integral boundary, and unimodular bases yield 28 free three-spheres plus a Moore M(Z/3,3). This is exhaustive finite mathematics, not partial search; no other graph is claimed.

originality.rationale: The final assertion is a graph-specific *homotopy equivalence*, not a generic statement that matching complexes have torsion. Jonsson analyzes matching complexes of complete graphs; Bayer–Jelic Milutinovic–Vega assume outerplanarity, impossible for a four-regular outerplanar graph; the indexed icosahedral and Grotzsch findings concern other graphs. No examined theorem entails the Chvatal Moore summand with 28 free three-spheres. Unindexed older calculations and the inaccessible original 1970 note remain genuine priority risks.

value.rationale: The Chvatal graph is a classical smallest triangle-free 4-regular 4-chromatic object, so the matching complex is an intrinsic and motivated topological invariant. Its exact Z/3 torsion and Moore summand distinguish it from the torsion-free Grotzsch matching complex and cannot be inferred from ordinary rational Betti numbers. A complete homotopy classification is useful even for this single canonical graph; this is not an unmotivated tiny parameter slice.
